name: Hu & Verdaguer Eq. (3.13): Gaussian Einstein-Langevin source of stochastic gravity; 'captures only partially the quantum nature' of fluctuations

source.located: arXiv:0802.0658v1 [gr-qc], 5 Feb 2008, B. L. Hu (Maryland) & E. Verdaguer (Barcelona), 'Stochastic Gravity: Theory and Applications' (Feb 2008 update of the 2003 Living Reviews review). Eq. (3.11)-(3.13) on p.10 (Sec. 3.2), Eq. (3.14)-(3.17) pp.11-12, Eq. published_statement: p.10, Sec. 3.2: 'N_abcd[g;x,y) = (1/2) <{t_ab[g;x), t_cd[g;y)}>, (3.11) ... t_ab[g;x) = T_ab[g;x) - <T_ab[g;x)>. (3.12) ... The bi-tensor N_abcd ... is real and positive semi-definite, as a consequence of T^R_ab being self-adjoint. ... Let us now introduce a Gaussian stochastic tensor field xi_ab[g;x) defined by the following correlators: <xi_ab[g;x)>_s = 0, <xi_ab[g;x) xi_cd[g;y)>_s = N_abcd[g;x,y), (3.13) where <...>_s means statistical average. The symmetry and positive semi-definite property of the noise kernel guarantees that the stochastic field tensor xi_ab ... is well defined. Note that this stochastic tensor captures only partially the quantum nature of the fluctuations of the stress-energy operator since it assumes that cumulants of higher order are zero.' It then sources the Einstein-Langevin equation (3.14) for a linear perturbation h_ab of a background g_ab that solves the semiclassical Einstein equation (3.7); its role is fixed by (3.16)-(3.17): the stochastic two-point correlations of h equal the SYMMETRIZED quantum two-point correlations to leading order in 1/N.
published_hypotheses: a real FREE (linear) scalar field of mass m, curvature coupling xi, action (3.1); 'we just assume a scalar field for simplicity' (p.7)
the field in a state |psi> with renormalized T^R_ab self-adjoint; N defined in that state (Eq. 3.11) -- not only the vacuum (the abstract's 'vacuum expectation value' is the special case)

N free of UV divergences for a LINEAR field at separated points (p.10); coincidence limit meaningful only as a distribution (p.10, p.12; Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur')
N real, symmetric and positive semi-definite -- the property that makes the Gaussian field (3.13) well defined (p.10)
GAUSSIAN: all cumulants of order > 2 set to zero -- the stated reason the source 'captures only partially the quantum nature' (p.10)
the background g_ab solves the semiclassical Einstein equations (3.7); xi_ab lives on that background and is independent of h (pp.10-11)
linear order in the metric perturbation h_ab (p.11, Eq. 3.14)
for N fields the correlator (3.13) is 1/N times one field's noise kernel; the stochastic/quantum correspondence (3.17) holds to leading order in 1/N (p.12)
what (3.13) is FOR: two-point (symmetrized) correlations of h (3.16)-(3.17), and the Feynman-Vernon identity (4.11); no claim is made about tail probabilities or the one-point law of T_ab
hypothesis_drift: MATCHES, not a drift: noise.py:133-134 'Hu & Verdaguer's N = <{t,t}>/2 is the FULL connected variance' agrees with Eq. (3.11) verbatim; for a real sampler f, N(f,f) = (1/2)<{t(f),t(f)}> = <t(f)^2> = Var_psi[T(f)] in any state, so 'full connected variance' is exact (t = T - <T>).

NORMALISATION DISCREPANCY IN THE LITERATURE, recorded not repaired, no effect on the tree: the same source's Sec. 5.2.1 Eq. (5.17) (p.29, from Phillips-Hu) writes 8N = <{t,t}>, and Bates 1305.3755 Eq. (4)/(7b) writes N = <{t,t}> with no 1/2. The tree follows (3.11) and in any case uses the variance directly (K_F from Var formula (V), controlled against FFR 1204.3570 Table I), so no figure depends on which normalisation of N is meant.

CAVEAT'S REASON CLAUSE OMITTED (noise.py:169-171): the tree quotes 'captures only partially the quantum nature' verbatim but not the clause that follows it, 'since it assumes that cumulants of higher order are zero'. Not a content drift: the tree's own H6/C1 split (noise.py:162-171, 22-34) states the stronger fact that the quantum spectral law has a hard floor where the Gaussian does not.

ADDED READING, disclosed by the tree: noise.py:46-53 and 344-360 read the ONE-POINT law of the worldline-smeared xi_00 as a probability of a density outcome, Prob(xi(f) <= -D) = erfc(z/sqrt2)/2. H&V define xi to reproduce symmetrized two-point correlations of h (3.16)-(3.17) and make no tail or one-point claim. The tree labels this 'a different reading of distribution, NOT H6' and calls it a 'surrogate' (noise.py:46-48, 166-171, 293-296), so it is not attributed to H&V; it remains the tree's reading, not the source's result.

BACKGROUND HYPOTHESIS HOLDS ONLY IN THE FLAT MODEL (implicit in the tree): H&V require g_ab to solve the semiclassical Einstein equations (3.7). Minkowski with the vacuum (<T^R> = 0, Lambda = 0) does, so the vacuum-kernel number is inside H&V's hypotheses as a FLAT figure. The corridor does not (its demand D is not <T^R> of any state, and H2 fails by b/l_G = 61.237, noise.py:36-44). The canonical entry lists 'flat (H2)'; the sentence at noise.py:46-53 gives the number 'at b = 1 m' without repeating the flat/SURVEY qualifier that governs section 0's corridor paragraph just above it (noise.py:36-44).

NOT A DRIFT: the tree's field (free scalar, minimal coupling xi = 0, m = 0 in the variance, noise.py:151-153) is inside H&V's (3.1) with xi = 0; single field (N = 1) rather than large N -- the large-N correspondence (3.17) is not used by the tree.

NOT A DRIFT: the tree takes the vacuum noise kernel only and states that for states with larger noise kernels the surrogate's probability is set by that kernel and NOT computed (noise.py:51-53, 226-227; EL_SURROGATE_NONVACUUM_COMPUTED = False).

later_literature.what: The vacuum distribution of a time-smeared stress tensor (2D CFT) is a shifted Gamma, alpha = c/24, with a hard lower floor equal to the optimal QEI bound; 84-89 percent of outcomes negative; 4D :phi^2: Lorentzian fitted exactly by alpha = 1/72 (Eq. 26); 4D energy density NOT a shifted Gamma, positive tail heavier. Confirms H&V's own caveat that the Gaussian source does not carry the quantum law; the tree already uses this (note [18]) for H6. Its Eq. (26) cumulants are reproduced exactly here (rederive C5).

later_literature.what: 4D moments of the smeared energy density grow like (3n-4)!, so the moments may not determine the distribution; skewed, heavy positive tail. Consistent with 'captures only partially'. Cited here via Bates 1305.3755 p.9 and via noise.py's own reading; not re-read this stage.

States that the Gaussian theory of Martin-Verdaguer/H&V truncates the influence functional at quadratic order (p.2) and proposes a non-Gaussian xi whose moments equal the symmetrized n-point functions of t_ab (conjecture Eq. 10); finds a point-smeared energy-density law with a hard negative cutoff and ~62 percent negative outcomes, 'markedly different from that predicted by Gaussian fluctuations' (p.8). Its details disagree with FFR (alpha = 1/2 vs 1/72). Extends, does not contradict, Eq. (3.13) as a definition; it also uses N = <{t,t}> without the 1/2 (normalisation discrepancy recorded above).

lacked_data: What the authors lacked in 2008: the full probability distribution of smeared stress-tensor measurements -- FFR 1004.0179 (2010) and 1204.3570 (2012) came later, and Bates 1305.3755 (2013) later still. Does having it change H&V's conclusion? NO, evidence: H&V never claimed the Gaussian source is the quantum law; p.10 says in so many words that it 'captures only partially the quantum nature ... since it assumes that cumulants of higher order are zero', and its stated job ((3.16)-(3.17), (4.11)) needs only the second cumulant, which the later work does not dispute (rederive B, C1: the smeared kernels are positive). The later data quantifies the caveat rather than overturning anything: skewness 12 sqrt(2) for the Lorentzian Wick square, and the Gaussian places 45 percent (phi^2) / 24 percent (the tree's rho) of its mass below a floor the quantum law never crosses (rederive C7, C8b). Does it change the TREE's conclusion? NO, evidence: the tree reads the Gaussian tail only as a labelled surrogate ('NOT H6'), and for the negative tail the later data moves in the direction that makes the tree's requirement stronger, not weaker -- under the quantum spectral law the probability at the demand is exactly 0 in the flat model (C1), and the surrogate gives exp(-10^141.916) > 0; either reading leaves 'restating the demand column about a distribution refuses exactly what the expectation-value column refuses' intact. No moved numerical datum exists for a definition; the tree's number depends only on G (unchanged CODATA 2018 -> 2022), exact hbar and c, and the tree's own K_F and D.
grade_evidence: Statement: noise.py's quotes ('captures only partially the quantum nature', 'N = <{t,t}>/2') match 0802.0658 p.10 Eqs. (3.11)-(3.13) verbatim (READ). Hypotheses as used: the tree applies (3.13) only to the free minimally coupled scalar in the Minkowski vacuum (inside H&V's (3.1) with xi = 0; Minkowski vacuum solves (3.7)), explicitly as a surrogate distinct from the quantum spectral law (H6), and refuses non-vacuum kernels. Re-derivation: 22/22 checks pass -- the tree's exp(-10^141.91579497495206) reproduced independently to 1e-14, its CORRECTED entry (not below exp(-10^142)) confirmed, the smeared noise-kernel variances exact in sympy, and H&V's caveat confirmed quantitatively by an exact third cumulant that also reproduces FFR 1004.0179 Eq. (26). Data: no datum of the definition exists; G unchanged in CODATA 2022; the exponent sits 0.084 below 142 and 0.916 above 141, needing K_F to move by x0.82 or x8.2 to cross. Named caveats that do not lower the grade: (i) the one-point tail reading is the tree's, not H&V's (disclosed as 'NOT H6'); (ii) H&V's background hypothesis holds only in the flat model, and noise.py:46-53 does not repeat the flat/SURVEY qualifier beside the number; (iii) a normalisation discrepancy for N exists inside the source (3.11 vs 5.17) and across the literature (Bates Eq. 4), with no effect on any tree figure.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the surrogate figure exp(-10^141.916) were quoted as a physical probability, or as holding on the curved corridor, without its 'NOT H6' and flat (H2) qualifiers -- H&V's (3.13) is defined on a background solving the semiclassical equations and claims only second-order statistics; the corridor satisfies neither H2 nor (3.7). DATA-DEPENDENT only if K_F (the tree's own measurement) or D moved by the factors above (x0.82 / x8.2 in K_F). WRONG would need a computed contradiction of (3.11)-(3.13) (e.g. a non-positive smeared noise kernel), which none of the 22 checks found. Reading gr-qc/0307032 (the 2004 version FFR cite) could only affect the attribution, not the definition.
